title: DRBench: A Realistic Benchmark for Enterprise Deep Research
claim: An end-to-end benchmark pipeline grounds an agent in persona and enterprise context, has it mine public and private data, and scores its report.
layout: Dense single panel, left-to-right with a loop back along the bottom; numbered circles 1-5 mark stages, dashed boxes group data sources, and arrows link them
description: A single wide diagram with five numbered stages. At left, a blue Task Context column holds a research question, a company and a persona as peach boxes with icons. Arrows carry this context to a robot agent in the center. The agent connects upward to a web-browsing icon for public data. It connects rightward to a pink enterprise environment box listing NextCloud, File System, Mattermost and RoundCube. A dashed yellow Task Data box at upper right lists chats, emails, slides, spreadsheets and documents, and an arrow loads these into the environment. The agent's output goes down to a blue Structured Report with red citations. Three peach evaluation boxes (Factuality, Report Quality, Insight Recall) sit at lower center. A dashed Injected Insights box at lower right feeds ground-truth insights into them. Pink numbered circles show the order.
caption: \method pipeline. \circledigit{1} The Task Context defines the deep research question grounded by the company and persona given to the agent. \circledigit{2} Task Data, including both distractor and injected groundtruth insights in different formats (PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, chats, etc.) are loaded into the enterprise environment's applications. \circledigit{3} The \method Agent accesses both public web sources and local enterprise data to extract relevant insights for the research question. \circledigit{4} It produces a structured research report, which is \circledigit{5} evaluated for Insight Recall (detecting injected groundtruth insights), Factuality (verifying claims are correctly cited), and Report Quality.
abstract: We introduce DRBench, a benchmark for evaluating AI agents on complex, open-ended deep research tasks in enterprise settings. Unlike prior benchmarks that focus on simple questions or web-only queries, DRBench evaluates agents on multi-step queries (for example, "What changes should we make to our product roadmap to ensure compliance with this standard?") that require identifying supporting facts from both the public web and private company knowledge base. Each task is grounded in realistic user personas and enterprise context, spanning a heterogeneous search space that includes productivity software, cloud file systems, emails, chat conversations, and the open web. Tasks are generated through a carefully designed synthesis pipeline with human-in-the-loop verification, and agents are evaluated on their ability to recall relevant insights, maintain factual accuracy, and produce coherent, well-structured reports. We release 100 deep research tasks across 10 domains, such as Sales, Cybersecurity, and Compliance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of DRBench by evaluating diverse DR agents across open- and closed-source models (such as GPT, Llama, and Qwen) and DR strategies, highlighting their strengths, weaknesses, and the critical path for advancing enterprise deep research. Code and data are available at https://github.com/ServiceNow/drbench.
